q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not drop — net sales on 2026-10-13 were ₹91,220 vs ₹40,119 on 2026-10-12 (+127.3%); the business saw a large one‑day increase, not a decline.

What changed (biggest impacts)
- Orders rose from 26 → 45 (+73.1%), so much of the lift came from volume increase.  
- Net AOV rose from ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31.4%), so each order was worth more as well.  
- Ad spend increased from ₹38,661 → ₹50,442 (+30.5%) and moved together with sessions; the data shows correlation but does not prove causation.  
- Returns/return revenue fell versus the usual (product return revenue was effectively 0 on 2026-10-13 vs normal), which raised gross sales contribution that day.  
- Discounts were higher (₹1,553 → ₹5,173), but this was smaller than the sales lift.

Quick read on certainty: the diagnostics found no single upstream cause labeled “supported_cause” — the change is within the metric’s normal historical range and the engine reports these as co‑movements (orders, AOV, ad spend) rather than an identified causal edit.

Worth checking: drill sales by campaign and by product (orders × AOV drivers) to see which ads or SKUs concentrated the volume and AOV uplift.
